security_audit.summary: Most external command detections are false positives caused by Markdown fences and inline payload examples, not executable skill code. Several network and blocker findings are confirmed because the skill includes sensitive file access, SSRF, tracking callback, XSS, path traversal, DoS, and rate limit evasion guidance. The content is dual use and requires strict authorization guardrails before publication.

remediation.suggestion: Remove file:///etc/passwd examples or replace them with harmless fixture paths in a local lab environment.
Replace iplogger.com and attacker-controlled callback examples with owned test infrastructure and explicit consent requirements.
Add clear authorization gates and remove or constrain brute force, DoS, and IP rotation recommendations.
Limit SSRF and localhost port examples to controlled lab targets with safe mock services.

content.user_title: Test API Security With Fuzzing Workflows
content.value_statement: API testers need structured ways to find authorization, injection, and endpoint weaknesses. This skill provides a checklist-driven workflow for authorized REST, SOAP, and GraphQL assessments.
actual_capabilities: Maps REST, SOAP, and GraphQL API testing steps into a single workflow.
Lists endpoint discovery methods using Swagger, OpenAPI, archives, and wordlists.
Provides IDOR, method tampering, rate limit, and content type test ideas.
Covers GraphQL introspection, batching, nested query, and injection checks.
Includes quick references for common API vulnerability classes and testing tools.
limitations: It is a guidance document, not an automated scanner.
It does not verify authorization or legal scope for a target.
Some payloads are high risk and can harm systems if misused.
It does not replace manual validation by a qualified security tester.

use_cases.title: Prepare an Authorized API Test
use_cases.description: Build a scoped checklist for endpoint discovery, authentication checks, and version comparisons before testing starts.

use_cases.title: Review Bug Bounty API Targets
use_cases.description: Plan focused IDOR, GraphQL, and rate limit tests for targets that are inside program scope.

use_cases.title: Improve API Defense Coverage
use_cases.description: Use the vulnerability checklist to compare application controls against common API attack paths.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic API Test Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for an authorized target.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a safe API security test plan for this authorized target. Include discovery, authentication checks, IDOR checks, and evidence to collect.

prompt_templates.title: Design IDOR Test Cases
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these API endpoints and design authorized IDOR test cases. Separate low impact checks from tests that require explicit approval.

prompt_templates.title: Assess GraphQL Exposure
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a GraphQL security assessment workflow for this schema or endpoint list. Cover introspection, batching, nested queries, and access control.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize API Findings
prompt_templates.prompt: Given these API test observations, prioritize likely vulnerabilities, explain impact, list validation steps, and note any tests that must not continue.

output_examples.input: A tester asks for an API bug bounty checklist for a scoped REST service.
output: Discovery checklist covering documentation, versions, and hidden endpoints.
Authorization checks for object references and role changes.
Evidence plan with request, response, account context, and impact notes.

output_examples.input: An application team wants to understand GraphQL risk before launch.
output: Assessment outline for schema exposure, query depth, batching, and mutations.
Recommended guardrails for rate limits, authorization checks, and error handling.
Manual review steps for sensitive fields and role-specific access.

output_examples.input: A report draft includes several possible API issues.
output: Prioritized finding list by impact and confidence.
Validation questions for scope, authorization, and reproducibility.
Remediation themes for access control, input validation, and monitoring.

best_practices: Confirm written authorization and scope before any active testing.
Start with low impact checks and stop when a payload may harm availability or data.
Record clear evidence without collecting more sensitive data than necessary.
anti_patterns: Testing production systems without explicit permission.
Using brute force, DoS, or rate limit evasion outside the approved scope.
Copying exploit payloads into live targets without impact controls.

faq.question: Is this an automated API scanner?
faq.answer: No. It is an instructional workflow and checklist for authorized API security testing.

faq.question: Can this be used with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Does it support GraphQL testing?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes GraphQL introspection, IDOR, injection, batching, nested query, and XSS testing ideas.

faq.question: Does it prove a target is in scope?
faq.answer: No. Users must verify authorization, program rules, and legal scope before using any technique.

faq.question: What are the main risks?
faq.answer: Some examples involve sensitive file access, SSRF, brute force, DoS, and rate limit evasion.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: It is intended for trained security testers working under a defined engagement or bug bounty scope.
